summary: Tenant-anchored model pin oscillation during health-probe spike causes mixed-variant responses
description:
Issue summary:
Customer EduScale reports intermittent mixed responses from two model variants after they pinned sessions to gpt-small-1.1 for a gradual canary. The problem started after an automated health-probe spike from an autoscaler event; session-level anchors appeared to oscillate between primary and fallback variants.

Impact:
- Affected ~12% of requests from the customer’s production tenant in us-west for approximately 18 minutes.
- Some chat sessions received tokens generated by the fallback variant (quantized) while the tenant believed sessions were pinned to the non-quantized model.
- Customer reports visible quality regressions for short-lived conversational flows.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod (us-west)
- Tenant: eduscale-prod-1 (dedicated pool)
- Routing policy: tenant-pinned -> canary-weighted (10%) -> fallback path to gpt-small-1.1-quant when capacity constrained

Steps to reproduce (observed locally by ops):
1) Trigger a short synthetic traffic spike (200 rps sustained for 30s) against tenant route with a pinned session cookie.
2) Simulate an autoscaler health-probe spike that induced controller probe retries around the same time.
3) Observe edge-proxy logs showing repeated pin reevaluation for the same session token and alternating route decisions.

Observed behavior:
- Pin handshake succeeded initially, then repeated health probes caused coordinator to mark a subset of nodes as degraded.
- Edge-proxy retry logic re-evaluated pins and sometimes selected the fallback (quantized) variant for new requests within the same session ID.
- No 5xx errors surfaced; responses completed but from unexpected variant.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant-level pin should remain anchored until explicit unpin or TTL expiry. Health-probe jitter should not cause mid-session variant switches.

Attachments:
- Edge logs (truncated) and coordinator metrics attached to ticket (log IDs: edg-logs-1132, coord-metrics-1132).

The debounce allowed coordinator to emit a degraded state for short windows; the pin reconciliation logic treated that as a candidate to re-resolve routing, which then picked fallback variants under our current prioritization rules.

2026-03-14 12:30 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Implemented temporary mitigation: extended pin-lease grace window (edge-side) for the tenant to 60s and disabled aggressive edge re-resolve for degraded->healthy transitions. Observing reduction in oscillations in monitoring. Awaiting customer validation.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: health-probe jitter + coordinator debounce window triggers re-evaluation of pinned sessions leading to edge fallback selection.
Logs show coordinator flagged two GPUs as degraded at 08:58:03 UTC, recovered at 08:58:26 UTC. During this 23s window > 200 requests tied to pinned sessions hit routing re-resolve path.
Edge-proxy's re-resolve path currently treats 'stale anchor' as eligible for fallback selection; this logic is by-design for availability but interacts poorly with tenant-level explicit pins.
Related config: pin-lease-ttl=300s, pin-grace-window-edge=10s (default). Increasing to 60s reduces occurrences in canary testbed.
No evidence of client token rotation or cookie corruption. CDN layer had no errors; all responses were 200 from either variant.
Potential race with autoscaler probe schedule aligning with canary traffic bursts; creating follow-up runbook step to avoid probe alignment with high canary weight windows.
resolution:
Workaround applied: edge pin-grace-window temporarily increased to 60s for eduscale-prod-1 and aggressive re-resolve on degrade->healthy transitions disabled for 2 hours. Monitoring shows oscillation count dropped by ~88% after mitigation.

Permanent fix plan (tracking):
- Change routing reconciler so explicit tenant pins take precedence over short-lived degraded flags (< 30s) unless pin-ttl expired (PR in progress: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7890).
- Add coordinator metric and alert for 'pin-reconcile-retries' and expose to Console for tenant owners.
- Update canary runbook to include staggered health-probe windows during tenant-pinned gradual rollouts.

Follow-ups assigned to Engineering (Priya Nair) and SRE (Marco Rivera). ETA for code change and canary: 2026-03-20. Customer notified and asked to re-open if further regressions are observed.
